points.description: States that a prototype program is used to simulate (model, imitate, imitate the behaviour of, or try out the behaviour of) parts of the software product that is to be built — i.e. it stands in for portions of the desired product so their behaviour can be examined. Accept paraphrases such as 'a working model of part of the system used to see how it behaves', 'a preliminary version that imitates what part of the final software will do'. Do not accept answers that only say a prototype is 'a first/trial version' or 'used to test the program' without any reference to simulating or modelling the behaviour of part of the intended product.
points.partial_credit: Half to most marks for an answer that gives only one half of the idea: either simulation/modelling of behaviour with no mention that it covers portions of the product, or 'a model of part of the product' with no mention of simulating its behaviour.

levels.says: Says a prototype is a preliminary/trial/working version of the software used to test or try out ideas, but does not say it simulates or models the behaviour of part of the desired product.

States that the prototype simulates or models behaviour (or is a model of part of the product) but omits one element — e.g. says it simulates the behaviour of the software without saying it is only portions of it, or says it is a model of part of the product without saying behaviour is simulated.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the idea that the prototype simulates or models the behaviour of portions of the desired software product. Part marks are given when only one element is present (simulating behaviour, or modelling part of the product) or when the answer is a vague 'trial version used for testing'. Answers that give no link to simulating/modelling behaviour of part of the intended product earn nothing.
